chapters.title: Chapter 112: Map Investment
paragraphs: Kai didn’t have any more Survivor Medals or even usable Energy Cores, so the Discount Vouchers were basically useless for now.
However, he could still purchase items using his Experience Points, and that alone made his heart race.
He forced himself to stay calm, controlling the excitement inside him.
The EMP grenade was tempting, but the price tag of 10,000 EXP was far beyond what he was willing to pay.
He shook his head. "It’s good but too expensive... I’ll pass for now."
Then, his gaze shifted to the box of preserved spices. The box was marked at 1,000 EXP, and Kai believed that it was a very reasonable price.
As a matter of fact, it seemed to be a very cheap product!

Thankfully, he had eliminated a large number of mutants earlier, so he had plenty of surplus points. More importantly, spices meant flavor. It was a way to improve their meals, and it might even help boost morale.
"This is worth it," he muttered.
Then his eyes moved to the rolled scroll tied with leather. The note beneath it said it was a map and marked the price at 4,000 EXP.
He couldn’t see the details inside, but the cost alone told him it was something extraordinary.
"It has to be important. But this is the map of this place, right? Not a random location?" Kai asked as he was seriously considering purchasing it now.
However, the Gene Trader didn’t answer.
Still, Kai didn’t want to let it go. After all, he believed that the Gene Trader wouldn’t sell a useless map. Even if it was a Treasure Map instead of the regional map, he didn’t mind at all!
’Am I going to level down because of this?’
The thought gnawed at him, but he knew how this piece of paper could give him what he needed to be at an advantage against the A.I. Army...
He had a feeling that it was worth the risk. Unlike Diego and Santiago, whose information had been unreliable, this was a direct trade from the Gene Trader. He could definitely trust it!
Kai straightened his back and spoke firmly. "I’ll take the spices first."
Immediately, a system notification appeared...
[ Instruction: Hold the item and touch the purple crystal to complete payment. ]
’So that’s how it works.’

Kai picked up the box of spices. He held it tightly, then reached out with his other hand and touched the glowing crystal. The moment his fingers brushed the surface, a sudden drain surged through him.
[ 1,000 Experience Points deducted. ]
[ Current EXP Balance: 3,450 ]

"Oh? I can see it clearly here." Kai muttered in surprise. After all, the visible Experience Points disappeared after reaching Level 10. This time, however, the Experience Points could finally be seen!
In any case, the items selected didn’t go to his inventory. It means that he must carry the box of spices with him, unless he wants to use his available Inventory Slots.
Still, Kai was already satisfied with this.
Next, he reached for the scroll. His fingers trembled slightly as he touched the crystal again.
[ 4,000 Experience Points deducted. ]
Then another message appeared...
[ Level Down: From Level 17 to Level 16 ]
[ Attribute Loss: Spirit -1, Health -5 ]
[ Adjustment Applied. ]
[ Current EXP Balance: 14,450 ]
"Oh well..." Kai expected this much, but he didn’t mind.
’It’s actually 15,000 experience points to reach Level 17, huh... No wonder it was so hard to level up.’
Perhaps, if not for the numerous Mutants who had attacked them, he wouldn’t have had enough Experience Points at all.
"Ahhh... Mutants? Wait--"
Kai froze as he realized something...
Perhaps, he should be asking Russel and the others to trigger the traps to attract mutants, so that he could get more Experience Points!
But as he reached this thought, he suddenly recalled the mutants attacking their New Haven-45...
’Don’t tell me...’

Kai straightened his back as he realized that there might have been a Gene Trader near their base, and perhaps, one of their residents unknowingly entered its territory, forcing the mutants to come out and attack them!
"That explains their sudden appearance!" Kai spoke up in realization.
It seemed that he would have to search the surroundings of the shelter once he was able to return.
For now, however, his attention turned to the map...
Kai carefully untied the strip of leather holding the scroll together.
His hands trembled slightly as he unrolled it...
At first glance, he realized it wasn’t a world map, nor a continental chart of the Versailles Continent.
Instead, the map only covered the Mavis Republic as written on the scroll.
It was his first time learning about the name of this land.

In any case, the next thing he noticed was the southern edge of the map. Apparently, it was marked by the sea, which meant Kai and his group were currently at the lower part of the Versailles Continent.
Soon, his attention was drawn to the legends and notes scattered across the map.
Each symbol carried a meaning that could be found at the bottom right of the map.
The first one he noticed was the head of an android, sketched in sharp lines.
According to the legend, this symbol represented an A.I. City.
Without a doubt, they were massive strongholds of machine soldiers, places no ordinary survivor could hope to enter.
Next was the golden star. The note beside it identified it as a top-class human shelter!
But Kai’s heart sank when he realized there was only one golden star on the entire map. Just one sanctuary of that caliber existed in the Republic of Mavis.
He continued scanning.

There were red skulls, denoting danger zones where mutant hordes, scavengers, or lawless people could gather in overwhelming numbers. And scattered across the parchment were blue droplets, symbols for clean water sources, rivers, and reservoirs.
Then, at this point, Kai found the area called Haven Shelters in the eastern territory of the map!
’Ohh... We should be around here...’
Kai immediately knew that their previous Haven-45 Shelter and other Haven Shelters were around this area!
He wanted to guess the rough location of the New Haven-45!
But then his gaze shifted again... He just realized that within the same eastern territory, there were four android heads marked close to one another.
It means that four A.I. Cities were actually surrounding the Haven Region!

chapters.title: Chapter 113: The Return
paragraphs: Kai was stunned as he immediately checked the area...
"Four cities, huh..."
Then, he checked the rest of the Mavis Republic... According to the map, there were five other regions aside from the Haven Region where the Haven Shelters are located.
There were Storm, Grid, Frontier, Origin, and Novel Regions.
These were the six regions of the Republic, and according to the map, there were a total of 24 large A.I. Cities within these regions!
Unfortunately, he still couldn’t find the location of their New Haven Shelter. After all, they were not near a huge lake, river, or any iconic location that the map could place.
Still, he’d probably learn more about this soon enough...
He didn’t regret this purchase at all, even if he leveled down in the process.
The information he had gained was priceless.
The locations of the A.I. Cities alone were worth the price, but the map revealed far more than that.

There were notes about mech graveyards, places where the wreckage of destroyed machines lay in piles. Such sites could be dangerous, but they were also treasure troves of salvageable parts, rare alloys, and forgotten technology.
There were also markings for human cities, scattered across the Republic.
Kai frowned as he studied them. "Human cities...? Open ones?" he muttered.
He was skeptical. If there truly were functioning human cities, why hadn’t the A.I. Army destroyed them already?

He had seen the Ascendant Unit with his own eyes. It was a monster capable of fighting multiple high‐level augmented humans at once. If such a weapon existed, then no human city could stand unchallenged.
Kai shook his head. "This map might be outdated. Those cities... they’re probably ruins now."

Still, even ruins had value. They could hold supplies, hidden caches, or even survivors clinging to life. The map also marked resource zones like mines, important factories, and energy stations. Each one was a potential lifeline for rebuilding, or a trap set by the A.I.
Kai exhaled as he rolled his map.
He then turned his gaze back to the Gene Trader. The cloaked figure remained silent, unmoving, as if it had already forgotten the transaction.
Kai bowed slightly, a gesture of respect. "Thank you," he said quietly.
With that, he finally decided to leave.
As he stepped out of the chamber, the dim light gave way to the familiar faces of his companions. It was already quite dark.
Russel and the others were there waiting anxiously.
When they saw Kai emerge, their expressions broke into smiles.
They knew. He had succeeded in making a transaction with the Gene Trader.
"Alright... It’s time to leave." Kai said.
Though he planned to return to Haven-62 to get Alfie and Farrah, that would have to wait until later.
Even though the night had already fallen, the team moved without difficulty. Each of them wore night‐vision goggles that all came from Kai’s Stealth Gift Packs...
Russel, Gabby, and Dylan took the lead, scanning the path ahead...
Then, Atom walked behind, covering their rear.
As for Kai, he stayed in the middle of the formation so he could react properly depending on their situation.
The journey back to New Haven‐45 was quite uneventful. There weren’t any lurking Sentinels, Swarmers, or any Mechanical Soldiers around.
Yet the team pressed forward cautiously.
Soon, the familiar outline of their shelter came into view.

New Haven‐45 was dark, with its exterior completely devoid of lights. The blackout was intentional. It was a precaution to avoid detection by the A.I. Army. To the machines, even a flicker of light could be a signal, a target.
Inside the main building, however, several flashlights had been turned on...
They had boxes of battery supplies after all.
Inside, Augustine’s team had already returned, and their expressions were heavy with disappointment.
As expected, his group had failed to locate a Gene Trader even after a day of search...
However, Kai soon revealed the good news.
"We found one," he said simply.
The words surprised and excited everyone.
Claire, Wallace, Ralph, and Victor all turned toward him, waiting for him to reveal what he had discovered.
First, Kai unrolled the scroll slightly, showing them the parchment.
"This is one of the items I obtained... A map."
Gasps filled the room.

Then, before they could properly analyze the map, Kai explained what he had seen... the system-like store, the Gene Enhancement Serums, the Gene Weapons, the Pills, and other items that could be bought by either Medals or Cores!
He also mentioned the peddling of the Gene Trader that only accepts Experience Points!
"Experience Points?" Claire repeated in shock.
"What? They can take that too? What’s next, our Vitality Points or somethin?" Victor said with a chuckle.
For him, experience points weren’t easy to come by. After all, he wasn’t a combat expert but a mechanic.
He also gained experience points for doing his job as a mechanic, but the amount was too little if compared to killing enemies...
After that, Kai finally revealed the prices of the Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum...
"Four Survivor Medals..."
Claire’s jaw dropped...
The others also looked at Kai, stunned.
After a few seconds, Wallace muttered under his breath, "So Diego and Santiago... they really did overcharge us."
Ralph clenched his fists. "Those wandering merchants sold us Gene Enhancements at ridiculous prices. They sold it for 15 Survivor Medals! Compared to this... compared to the Trader’s store..."
He couldn’t even complete his sentence.
Victor shook his head in disbelief. "We were scammed."

Kai chuckled softly, though his tone carried no malice. "Not scammed. Just overpriced. They were merchants, after all. They sold what they had, at the price they thought they could get. The Gene Trader is different. It’s basically part of the system itself."
The others fell silent, digesting his words.
Finally, after everyone calmed down, Kai revealed the Status Crystal that he bought for 3 Survivor Medals.

[ Status Crystal: A rare crystal that reveals the complete status of the person who touches it. When activated, it displays their name, title, level, skills, and stats for exactly 10 seconds before fading.
Cooldown: After use, the crystal requires 30 seconds before it can be activated again.
Charge: 50 ]

[ Recharge Requirement: Once its charges reach zero, or even before that point, the crystal must be replenished by pouring Spirit Energy into it. Without this infusion, the crystal will remain dormant and unusable. ]

Then, before they could properly analyze the map, Kai explained what he had seen... the system-like store, the Gene Enhancement Serums, the Gene Weapons, the Pills, and other items that could be bought by either Medals or Cores!
He also mentioned the peddling of the Gene Trader that only accepts Experience Points!
"Experience Points?" Claire repeated in shock.
"What?
They can take that too?
What’s next, our Vitality Points or somethin?" Victor said with a chuckle.
For him, experience points weren’t easy to come by.
After all, he wasn’t a combat expert but a mechanic.
He also gained experience points for doing his job as a mechanic, but the amount was too little if compared to killing enemies...
After that, Kai finally revealed the prices of the Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum...
"Four Survivor Medals..."
Claire’s jaw dropped...
The others also looked at Kai, stunned.
After a few seconds, Wallace muttered under his breath, "So Diego and Santiago... they really did overcharge us."
Ralph clenched his fists.
"Those wandering merchants sold us Gene Enhancements at ridiculous prices.
They sold it for 15 Survivor Medals!
Compared to this... compared to the Trader’s store..."
He couldn’t even complete his sentence.
Victor shook his head in disbelief.
"We were scammed."
Kai chuckled softly, though his tone carried no malice.
"Not scammed.
Just overpriced.
They were merchants, after all.
They sold what they had, at the price they thought they could get.
The Gene Trader is different.
It’s basically part of the system itself."
The others fell silent, digesting his words.
Finally, after everyone calmed down, Kai revealed the Status Crystal that he bought for 3 Survivor Medals.
[ Status Crystal: A rare crystal that reveals the complete status of the person who touches it.
When activated, it displays their name, title, level, skills, and stats for exactly 10 seconds before fading.
Cooldown: After use, the crystal requires 30 seconds before it can be activated again.
Charge: 50 ]
[ Recharge Requirement: Once its charges reach zero, or even before that point, the crystal must be replenished by pouring Spirit Energy into it.
Without this infusion, the crystal will remain dormant and unusable. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 114: Status of the Residents
paragraphs: "You said three Survivor Medals? I think this is worth the price." Claire muttered as she studied the crystal.
"That’s true. This is a good investment." Wallace added.
At this time, Terrence also came forward and learned about its full description.
"Whoa~ This is nice... You want to see their stats? That’s good," Terrence said, realizing Kai’s true intention. He understood that Kai was planning something for the residents of the shelter.
This wasn’t just for entertainment but for strategic purposes.
Kai nodded firmly.
Then he called out, "Russel... you go first. Touch this sphere."
Russel didn’t hesitate and followed his instructions.
He stepped forward, placed his hand on the crystal, and immediately a glowing screen appeared before everyone.
[ Name: Russel ]
[ Title: Scout ]
[ Level: 7 ]
[ Spirit: 32 / 32 ]
[ Physique Rating: E+ ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Silent Steps Lv0 ]
The group, especially the residents who had never seen the system, was shocked at its presence.
Indeed, it wasn’t impressive compared to Kai’s stats or those of the Earth Survivors, but for the residents of this world, it was shocking.
They had never seen their own numbers before. Unlike Kai and the others from Earth, they didn’t have a system interface. This crystal was their only way of knowing their true capabilities.
Russel blinked at the display, stunned at the fact that he actually had a skill!
"So... this is me?"
Gabby leaned closer and also noticed it.
"Whoa... My friend! You’ve got Silent Steps! Even if it’s level zero, that’s still something!"
Dylan chuckled. "Scout fits you perfectly, Russel. No wonder you’re always sneaking ahead."
Excitement rippled through the room. For the first time, they could measure themselves!
Of course, Kai didn’t just ignore this. He felt excited as well, so he took out the sketch pad and his pencil that came from his Enhanced Entertainment Gift Pack.
Then, he listed the information in his paper. In any case, he gestured for the others to try it as well.
"Alright... Next!"
Soon, more stepped forward. Mila, the chief of the Sanitation Crew from the Support Units, placed her hand on the crystal.
[ Name: Mila ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Spirit: 20 / 20 ]
[ Physique Rating: E- ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Quick Learner Lv0 ]
Mila gasped, covering her mouth. "I... I have a skill? Quick Learner?"
Kai nodded. This was definitely useful information.
He also just realized that everyone had a different starting point in their Spirit Points and Health Points.
It was probably related to their Physique Rating, but Kai wasn’t exactly sure as well.

"This is a good passive skill. It’s extremely valuable. It means you’ll adapt faster to training, new tasks, or even combat techniques. With the right guidance, you’ll definitely grow stronger at a pace others can’t match."
Her eyes shone with pride. "So... it means I can change my role if I study it? Maybe I can become a marksman?"
Kai smiled. "That’s up to you."
With that said, another familiar figure stepped forward.
It was Irene, the head nurse from the Medic Division. She also felt excited and touched the crystal, and her stats appeared:
[ Name: Irene ]
[ Title: Caregiver ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Spirit: 40 / 40 ]
[ Physique Rating: E ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Steady Hands Lv0 ]
Irene stared at the glowing text and muttered. "Steady Hands...? That’s my skill?"
The others leaned closer to check and nodded. None of them was surprised.
Claire saw this as well, and she immediately understood how it happened.
"That makes sense. You’ve always been calm and precise with your hands, especially when treating wounds."
Kai nodded.

"Yes. It’s an important passive skill. I can guess Steady Hands means you can perform delicate tasks without hesitating... whether it’s stitching injuries, handling fragile equipment, or maybe even aiming a weapon. You should try practicing with guns, too."
"Guns?" Irene repeated.

She also had a revolver, and he had certainly tried using it a few times. However, since she wasn’t part of the combat division, she had limited ammunition supplied to her. Because of that, she never had a chance to seriously practice it.
"That would be awesome. I want to be strong enough to protect myself." She added.
Kai smiled as he wrote this on his paper.

One by one, more residents tried. Members of the Security Division stepped forward. Their stats show modest levels, but useful passive skills like Observant Eyes, Firm Grip, and Quick Reflexes would show from time to time.
Then came the kitchen helper.

Kai didn’t think too much of him since he was probably no older than nineteen or twenty, and he looked unassuming. His dark hair was messy, and it was as if he would be blown away by a breeze because of his small frame.
He had certainly failed to consume enough gold liquid, unlike Russel and the others.
Nothing about him suggested strength or power.
And yet, the crystal’s display told a different story.
Indeed! Kai was shocked as soon as he saw the man’s stats
[ Name: Amer ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 4 ]
[ Spirit: 85 / 85 ]
[ Physique Rating: E- ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: None ]
Kai froze, staring at the numbers. "Eighty‐five Spirit... at Level 4?"
"That’s... amazing. Even Russel, who consumed far more enhancement, doesn’t have that much Spirit, right?" Claire added.
The others also murmured in shock, exchanging glances.
Russel recalled his 32 Spirit Points despite being Level 7. However, actually didn’t mind being compared, and as a matter of fact, he was happy with this result.
Kai then turned to observe Amer and asked how many gold liquid or Gene Enhancement Serums he consumed...
"Only four drops. They were given to me once by Sir Damon, one of Haven‐45’s former leaders, after I visited him at night. That’s all."
The room fell silent.
After a few moments, Kai nodded.

"That must’ve been difficult. Ahem... You have potential for sure. You’ll be receiving your first skill at Level 5, so I’ll be prioritizing you for the Gene Enhancement Serum." Kai said. He knew very well that if Amer obtained a decent Gene Skill, it might be worth nurturing him.
Still, Kai simply noted the information for now so he wouldn’t forget it.
And just like that, in about an hour, he had obtained everyone’s status.

chapters.title: Chapter 115: Amer and the Search
paragraphs: "It’s getting colder..." Amer muttered as he woke up before dawn...
His eyes opened to the dim glow of the emergency lamps that lined the shelter’s corridors.
As he looked around, he confirmed that the others were still asleep.
Apparently, the quarters he shared with three other men were a bit cramped.
Even the air had the scent of oil and rust that never truly faded from the walls.
Their beds were nothing more than wooden frames, but each had a sleeping bag laid across it. It was a gift from Kai.
Without those, the hard planks would have been unbearable. There were no cushions, no mattresses, no softness at all. Comfort was a luxury they couldn’t afford right now.
When Kai had first conquered this shelter, Amer remembered how lifeless it had been. The halls were filled with unmoving Sentinels, with their metallic bodies frozen in place like statues.
Spare parts littered the floors like blades, gears, batteries, coils of wire, and containers of grease stacked in corners. It hadn’t been built for humans at all.
This place was basically once a base of the A.I. Army, a depot for machines...
"Another day of work..." Amer muttered as he slowly sat up to stretch his body.
Amer still recalled the eerie silence of those first days in this shelter.

The place had felt more like a graveyard than a home. But somehow, within just a few days, Kai had transformed it. He didn’t know how Kai did it... where the food came from, how weapons appeared, or why supplies seemed endless.
Kai had powers that defied explanation, pulling resources out of nowhere.
Even simple items like flashlights, firestarters, water buckets, books, bandages, painkillers, a compass, a whistle, and many more, Kai has them!
Amer sometimes joked to himself that Kai was selling his soul to some unseen force, but deep down, he knew it was something far more mysterious.
Whatever the truth, Kai’s abilities had kept them alive. Guns, food, smoke grenades, sleeping bags, and even a small camping tent, all of it had come from him.
Amer then rubbed the sleep from his eyes.
As he slowly moved.
His companions were still asleep, so he quietly rolled up his sleeping bag, careful not to wake them, and slipped out of the quarters.
The shelter was quiet at this hour, and their lights were only relying on the battery-powered emergency lights. Of course, there were also some flashlights scattered everywhere that anyone could use.

Firstly, Amer made his way to the washroom, where a crude system of pipes carried water from the tanks... Well, there was already some water supply here since even the A.I. Army needed a water supply.
Then, he bathed quickly, shivering as the cold water ran over his skin, but grateful nonetheless. Cleanliness was rare in this world, and Kai had insisted they maintain it.
After drying off, Amer headed to the kitchen.
His daily task was simple but important... preparing food for the others.
The shelves were stacked with canned goods, instant noodles, and other items like mayonnaise and granola bars. all scavenged or supplied by Kai.
But canned food or instant noodles alone were bland and heavy.
To make it better, Amer and the others had started cultivating a small garden outside the shelter led by Aurora...
They were now growing leafy greens and hardy vegetables.
It wasn’t much, but it added flavor and nutrition to their meals.
This morning, Amer opened a can of chicken broth and poured it into the pot.
He chopped a handful of leafy greens from yesterday’s harvest, adding them to the simmering liquid.
The aroma filled the kitchen, warm and comforting. He stirred slowly as he wanted the flavor to spread evenly...
Cooking wasn’t glamorous, but it was his way of contributing.
As he worked, Amer’s mind drifted back to last night. He remembered the glowing crystal, the Status Crystal Kai had revealed.
He remembered the shock on everyone’s faces when his stats appeared.
Eighty-five Spirit Points at Level 4.
It didn’t make sense.
He had only consumed four drops of the gold liquid, gifted to him once by Sir Damon, one of Haven‐45’s former leaders.
He wasn’t a fighter, wasn’t trained, wasn’t special.
And yet, the crystal had shown him something extraordinary.
Amer stirred the soup harder as his mind drifted.
Even Russel, a seasoned scout, had only 32 Spirit at Level 7. Amer’s number was more than double that.
He didn’t know what it meant, but he knew Kai was already planning to give him Enhancement Serums.
Could he really become someone important? Could he fight alongside the others, instead of just cooking soup and cleaning dishes?
This thought made him really excited about his future...
Clug... Clug...
The pot bubbled as steam started rising into the air. Amer tasted the broth, adjusted the taste by adding a little bit more water, and then he smiled faintly. It wasn’t much, but it was good enough.
Soon, the others would wake, and this simple meal would give them strength for another day.
Creak~
Suddenly, the kitchen doors opened.
"Ohh... You’re done with your duty, Amer?" Mila said as she saw Amer removing his apron.
"That’s quick... I guess we’re just going to clean the place now." Rudy, another kitchen helper, added.
"Ahh... I have some plans this morning, so I came in early." Amer replied as he scratched his head.
Apparently, Amer was the one tasked to cook for their morning meal, so he didn’t wait for the others.
As for their dinner, that would be for others to work on.
Later this evening, he would also be free to do anything...
Amer then slipped out of the kitchen as he planned to watch Victor dismantle another Sentinel in his workshop.
He knew that Victor would do this every morning, so he was already moving...
But then, he noticed the two full squads of Assault Team 1 and Team 2.
Apparently, they were being briefed by Kai, who was also up this early in the morning.
"I believe that the Gene Trader is nearby..." Kai declared as his eyes swept across the assembled fighters.
"That must be the reason why this shelter was attacked by mutants before. We’re not stopping until we find this person... no matter how long it takes!"

chapters.title: Chapter 116: Consent
paragraphs: The night before, Jonas and the rest of the Security Division received instructions from Wallace to patrol the surroundings early.
Apparently, the two Assault Teams would be searching for the Gene Trader that was supposedly just nearby.
"We have to gather early to help search the area?" Jonas asked Wallace.
"Not really... It’s the job of the Assault Teams. We’ll just stay in the vicinity of the shelter. Kai mentioned that there might be more mutants appearing. We need to be ready." Wallace answered.
"I see... I’ll wake up early then!" Jonas said, eager to do something for the shelter.
When he arrived here, he was with Terrence and Aurora from Haven-15.
Now, while Terrence was working hard at Assault Team B and Aurora was managing the garden because of her Talent, he was only doing some menial task like patrolling the wall.
’No... I can’t be negative... I’m sure that my time will come someday.’ Jonas reminded himself.
In any case, he checked his current status.
[ Name: Jonas ]
[ Title: Survivor ]
[ Level: 6 ]
[ Physique Rating: D- ]
[ Talent: Iron Stomach (Rare) ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Toxin Resistance Lv0 ]
[ Skill Points: 2 ]
His rare talent, Iron Stomach, defined him. It allowed him to eat almost anything without falling sick... Even if it was spoiled food, strange roots, or even meat that others wouldn’t dare touch.
Thanks to that, Jonas never worried about meals. While others fretted over rations, he could survive on scraps if needed.
It was a strange blessing, but in this world, it gave him a little advantage...
’I really wanted some kind of offensive Gene Skill. I hope they find the Gene Trader soon.’ Jonas thought as he had already learned from Kai that the Trader had Gene Skill Crystals.
The one with the guaranteed Passive Skill was only worth 2 Survivor Medals. However, if he wanted a chance of getting an Active Skill, he’d have to purchase the version worth 3 Survivor Medals.
That morning, Jonas woke up early to conduct his patrol...
At this time, he noticed that Amer was already heading toward the kitchen.
Jonas respected Amer’s diligence. The young man was always eager to contribute.

In any case, as part of the Security Division, Jonas was a wall defender. His daily life revolved around patrols, keeping watch for mutants or stray Sentinels, and helping reinforce the shelter’s defenses.
Sometimes, when things were quiet, he would even split wood for fuel using his hatchet...
It wasn’t glamorous, but it kept the fires burning and the shelter warm...
Soon, after a round of patrol, he finally saw the two Assault Teams being briefed by Kai. They were about to go outside to find the Gene Trader.
"Good luck, guys..." He muttered.
Three hours had passed since Kai sent out the Assault Teams.
Jonas had been waiting for any signs of mutants, but it seemed that they were safe today.
Indeed, the patrol had been uneventful... no mutants, no Sentinels, not even the faintest sound beyond the wind.
’Still nothing...’ he thought while scanning the horizon.
’If they haven’t returned by now, then they must have failed to find the Gene Trader nearby. Or maybe there’s none in the first place.’
The silence weighed on him. Jonas had hoped today would bring something new, something that might change his role in the shelter. But with no news, it felt like another wasted morning.
Suddenly, the sound of hurried footsteps broke the dullness.
A group of survivors rushed back through the gates, their faces pale...
"Where’s Kai?!" one of them shouted. "We need Kai right now!"
Jonas straightened as he heard. It must be really important.
"What happened?" Jonas asked.
"Ah... You see. Our mission was a success."
Apparently, they had found the Gene Trader. The man was hidden deep within the massive sewer system beneath the ruins. It was no wonder the Assault Teams had struggled...
The Trader had concealed himself so well that no one had thought to look underground.
Jonas felt so excited.
’The Gene Trader is here...’
But before the group could report further, the ground trembled beneath Jonas’s boots.
Thud... Thud...
Earthquake? Jonas thought, but the vibration was too deliberate. This wasn’t natural.
Then, he soon realized what was going on!
From beyond the perimeter, a mechanical entity emerges... It was a towering six meters tall! It may not be equipped with a sword or spear, or even a flamethrower, but it had clawed hands.
Jonas knew that this wouldn’t be easy... He had seen other Field Tyrants before, but this was different. This seemed more terrifying!
The ground shook violently as the six‐meter Tyrant Unit advanced...
Jonas gritted his teeth and ordered everyone to raise their weapons, but he knew this wasn’t a fight the Security Division could handle alone. The sheer size of the machine dwarfed the walls.
Then, a voice cut through the chaos.
"Clear his path!" Kai shouted as he gestured to Jonas’s group to move out of the way...
Then, after making a path, the Sentinel strode out from the gates.
In any case, Atom had a blade strapped across its back and a rifle already raised. He was ready!
Soon, the Field Tyrant charged forward!
Thud! Thud! Thud!
At this time, Jonas heard Kai instructing the Sentinel from a distance!
"Stop it from advancing! Protect the shelter!"
Atom heard this, and soon, its rifle spat a slug the size of a brick, smashing into the machine’s chest!
Bang!
The impact staggered the giant, and sparks burst from its armor. Another slug followed, tearing into its shoulder and forcing it back!
Kai was actually so calm in front of such monstrosity, and Jonas felt impressed!
Then, as the enemy kept coming, Jonas saw Atom drop the gun and drew the blade!
Apparently, the large Tyrant was strong enough to withstand Atom’s rifle shots!
Even Kai was amazed as he looked at the discarded rifle...
Its ammunition was just a slab of steel, but it had destroyed the previous Tyrants! It meant that this version of Tyrant was even stronger!
’I guess you’ll drop a decent loot later, right?’Kai thought as he saw Atom.

Apparently, the two Assault Teams would be searching for the Gene Trader that was supposedly just nearby.
"We have to gather early to help search the area?" Jonas asked Wallace.
"Not really...

We’ll just stay in the vicinity of the shelter.
Kai mentioned that there might be more mutants appearing.
We need to be ready." Wallace answered.
"I see...
I’ll wake up early then!" Jonas said, eager to do something for the shelter.

In any case, he checked his current status.

[ Title: Survivor ]
[ Level: 6 ]

[ Talent: Iron Stomach (Rare) ]
[ Active Skills: None ]

It allowed him to eat almost anything without falling sick...
Even if it was spoiled food, strange roots, or even meat that others wouldn’t dare touch.

Or maybe there’s none in the first place.’

You see.

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Trapped!
paragraphs: Thud!
With one powerful swing, Atom plunged the blade into the Tyrant’s core!
Everything happened so quickly as the Tyrant Mech convulsed, in a sense that it started jerking violently as if it was trying to throw Atom away.
However, that was not enough against Atom, who held tightly to its opened chest.
The Tyrant tried one last desperate attack... It raised its claws, but its movements were already sluggish at this point.
Even without Kai’s instruction. Atom attacked once again to end this!
Atom’s blade slashed and severed its neck!
Soon, the giant collapsed, crashing into the ground with a thunderous impact!
Boom!
[ Congratulations! You are the first Survivor to eliminate a Hooker Tyrant (C). ]
[ Hint: Only the first elimination of each C‐Grade and higher unit can provide special rewards! ]
[ You can select one reward: Instant Experience Potion x2, Energy Cores x2, Random Gift Pack x2, Survivor Medal x2, Material Treasure Chest x2 ]
"Ahhh..." Kai was stunned after seeing the message.
Another first elimination of its variant!
"Awesome... I hope there are more variants of you out there." Kai muttered as he certainly liked the reward that followed.
Although he had eliminated Tyrants before, he was actually able to find different versions of them.
They were the Field Tyrant that has a Furnace Core, the War Tyrant that uses Flamethrower, and this one, the Hooker Tyrant with impossibly hard claws that could destroy anything its clamped on.
"Wait..." Kai paused as he finally noticed that the Weapon Blueprint that was previously an option had disappeared and became Survivor Medals instead!
"Perfect..." Kai muttered as he saw Atom standing over the wreckage with its blade resting at its side.
Soon, Atom went to check the Tyrant’s core and stayed there for some time.
Once again, Kai had no idea what Atom was doing, but he just let it be for now.
In any case, every time Atom does this, it would get even stronger.
For now, Kai selected the Survivor Medal for the reward.
Meanwhile, Jonas and the rest of the wall defenders finally relaxed. They had survived another attack.
Then, as he was thinking about what Atom was doing, he heard someone call for him.

"Jonas! Drive the other truck! We will be looting a lot of things from that Tyrant!" Wallace shouted excitedly as he headed to get one of the armored cars. Then, he remembered something and called out to Mila, who had just come out of the mess hall.
"Hey, Mila! Get Victor here!"
"Got it!" Mila replied.
Jonas, on the other hand, was only surprised for a moment before he also replied.
"I’m on it... Wait for me!" Jonas replied.
Despite not having a license, he knew how to drive, so there was no issue at all.
Kai heard all of this and allowed them to work on it.
"Go... Secure the area. Make sure to follow Victor’s instructions," he ordered.

He knew that they were about to loot something good from this Hooker Tyrant. With that in mind, Victor, their only trustworthy mechanic, must lead the scavenging to avoid destroying the important parts of the Tyrant unit.
"I guess I can just visit Haven-62 a little later," Kai muttered to himself. Of course, he didn’t forget both Farrah and Alfie, who were probably waiting for him since yesterday.
He really planned to go there this morning, but the appearance of the Hooker Tyrant stopped him from doing so.
A few moments earlier, while Atom was clashing with the Hooker Tyrant near the shelter, the two Assault Teams led by Claire and Ralph had been scouring the surroundings...
Of course, the distant shrieks and deafening impacts of the Tyrant carried across the land.
Everyone in the teams froze for a moment, realizing their shelter was under attack.
They even considered stopping their mission since their shelter was definitely their priority here.
But before they could turn back, one of Ralph’s men stumbled into a strange clearing at the edge of the cemetery. The air felt heavier there, as if there was an unnatural presence.
"Captain... I think I found something," the scout called out and moved forward.
The moment he stepped deeper into the territory, however, the ground shifted. From the shadows of the tombstones and collapsed mausoleums, mutants began to crawl out!
Their terrifying forms emerged in droves.
The team froze.
"Ahhh! Sorry, captain!" The scout shouted.
"You..." Ralph was shocked.
This was both joyous and terrifying news. Joyous, because they had finally found the Gene Trader, hidden in the cemetery, just as Kai suggested.
Then, it was terrifying, because the one who had stepped inside wasn’t a Foreign Survivor or from Earth, but a native resident of this world... and that mistake had activated the Trader’s trap.
Dozens of mutants surged forward, clawing at the intruders.
"Hold the line!" Ralph shouted, raising his revolver. He fired into the nearest mutant and it hit its head!
Thud!
The creature collapsed, but more pressed in from every side.
Claire’s team rushed to assist. She swung her hatchet in a clean arc, splitting the skull of a mutant that had leapt too close.
"Don’t let them surround us!" she ordered.
In just a few seconds, the battle took its turn...
Hatchets were used as the fighters hacked down mutants at close range!
Unlike the Sentinels, their blades could easily cut through flesh and bone.
Then, after a few moments, revolvers were fired again and again!
Roar!
One mutant charged at Ralph with its claws extended.
He then sidestepped and buried his hatchet into its chest!
Thud!
[ +350 Experience Points. ]
After confirming the kill with the system notification, he kicked the body aside and fired at another that tried to flank him.
Bang!
At this point, even his men fought desperately with their revolvers.
Claire, on the other hand, moved and cut down one mutant after another just by relying on her physical strength... Even without the possession, she was actually strong enough to hold her ground!
In just a few moments, she eliminated a few more mutants alone...
Bang! Bang! Bang!
The cemetery became a killing ground. Mutants fell one after another, and soon, their bodies started piling among the broken tombstones.
Finally, after what felt like an eternity, the assault slowed.
Thud!
Soon, the last mutant collapsed with a revolver shot to the skull...
"Done! Do not approach the Gene Trader again!"

chapters.title: Chapter 120: Rows of Sentinels
paragraphs: Alfie and Farrah stepped forward quickly.
They were certainly relieved at the sight of the man they trusted to return.
"Kai," Farrah said, "this is Montez, the leader of Haven‐62. He’s the one who kept everyone together after the War Tyrant’s attack."
Farrah was actually thankful to this old man since he had also given her and Alfie the Gene Stimulant that increased their strength.
Thanks to that, the two of them managed to hold their ground until Kai’s superior Sentinel arrived.
On the other hand, Montez gave a short nod to Kai.
He wasn’t just impressed with Kai’s Sentinel but also with his physique.

Deep inside, he could tell that Kai was definitely one of those people capable of reaching the high-level Augmented Humans of the Versailles Ascendants, an elite order aiming to fight back against A.I. Civilization.
"We’ve done what you asked. The wreckage was guarded, and nothing was taken."
Just like that, Farrah and Alfie guided Kai toward the warehouse.
Inside, the survivors had stacked the crates neatly, each item catalogued.
Kai walked among them and scanned the contents.
There were alloy plating, cables, fragments of claws, and the cracked sensor lens were all accounted for.
Then his gaze fell on a crate holding several glowing Energy Cores. He crouched, inspecting them carefully, before nodding in approval.
"Good," Kai said.
Although Atom did something to the core, it seemed that they still found several more Energy Cores from the Tyrant Unit. As expected, the War Tyrant and the Hooker Tyrant were quite similar...
"You did well. These will be carried by the armored cars." Kai said.
This was the reason why he brought the two armored cars in the first place.
At this time, Farrah and Alfie glanced at each other...
It was time...
Farrah hesitated for a moment before she spoke. "Kai... the other six here want to come with us too."
Kai’s eyes narrowed slightly.
He had already decided to accept Alfie and Farrah because they were Foreign Survivors from Earth. They had Survivor Talents and a Leveling System that could make them undoubtedly stronger.
But the others were residents of this world. Trusting the two was already dangerous, so adding six could become a problem.
’Eight new residents, huh...’Kai mused as he considered the situation.
Eight new people could easily sabotage his shelter, especially when his numbers were only around forty.
If they were planning something bad, it would be hard to control them all.
Of course, the six survivors noticed his hesitation.
Farrah gestured for them to speak up and try to sell themselves.
One man stepped forward. "I can make traps. I’ve caught rats and snakes before. I can help with food. Trust me..."
Another survivor raised his hand. "I’m good with construction. Right... I’ve consumed fifteen drops of gold liquids that strengthened my body. I may not be a fighter, but I can lift heavy loads."
’Ohhh... Not bad.’ Kai mused as he knew that the 15 drops weren’t easy to obtain in a shelter with large population.
Then, a woman spoke next. "I know herbs. I can identify which ones are safe to eat, and which can be used to treat wounds. I can be useful, believe me..."
"I’ve worked with metal scraps before. I can repair simple tools and reinforce walls."
"I can scout. I know the land around Haven‐62. I can move quietly and warn of danger."
Finally, the last one stepped forward. "I can cook. I’ve kept people alive here with mushrooms and scraps. Give me better supplies, and I’ll make sure no one goes hungry."
The warehouse fell silent after their words. Each of them had offered something, trying to prove their worth.
’This...’
Kai stood still, weighing their skills against the risk.
All this time, Alfie and Farrah watched him closely, knowing this decision could change the lives of the six...
Kai stood in silence for a moment, weighing the risks against the skills the six had offered. Finally, he gave a short nod.
"All right," he said firmly. "You’ll come with us. But you’ll have to work harder than anyone else. My shelter is small, and every hand must contribute. If you fail, you won’t stay."
Relief washed over the group.
Alfie and Farrah exchanged quick smiles, knowing Kai had given them all a chance.
"Good," Kai continued. "For now, help us load the crates."
Immediately, everyone moved.
The survivors lifted boxes of alloy plating, claw parts, and cables, carrying them toward the armored cars.
Then, Atom joined in, making the task far easier. The Sentinel hoisted the heavier crates, including the ones holding the glowing Energy Cores, and placed them securely in the vehicles.
"That’s so useful."
"Amazing... Does it not run out of energy?"
"Can it speak?"
The sight of the machine working alongside them left the Haven‐62 survivors in awe.

They had many questions as well but Kai didn’t answer them since the operation time of Atom and other information related to it was top secret. The enemies shouldn’t know the weakness of his Sentinel, even if there was none.
Hours of careful cataloguing had now paid off.
In any case, nothing was missing, but Kai couldn’t take everything...
He had to be satisfied for now.
Kai inspected the cars one last time, satisfied that the most important parts were secured.
"Let’s move," he ordered.
The gates of Haven‐62 creaked open, and soon, the convoy rolled out.
The survivors who had chosen to stay behind watched silently, while the eight new recruits sat inside the armored cars.
Soon, the group moved to Kai’s shelter.
The journey was uneventful, but that was what they prayed for... Then, after some time, the familiar walls of New Haven‐45 came into view...
Of course, for Alfie, Farrah, and the six others, this would be their first time to see it... and the first thing they noticed was how terrifying it was!
"This..." Farrah was frozen.
As the armored cars rolled closer, they couldn’t help but feel nervous!
Along the walls of New Haven‐45 or Kai’s shelter, they saw rows of Sentinels!
They didn’t move, but their presence was enough to make the eight survivors uneasy.
Then, after passing through the gates, more Sentinels lined the pathways, standing at attention like silent soldiers!
"What?! You’re controlling so many Sentinels?" Alfie muttered, his voice filled with disbelief.

The survivors lifted boxes of alloy plating, claw parts, and cables, carrying them toward the armored cars.
Then, Atom joined in, making the task far easier.
The Sentinel hoisted the heavier crates, including the ones holding the glowing Energy Cores, and placed them securely in the vehicles.
"That’s so useful."
"Amazing...
Does it not run out of energy?"
"Can it speak?"
The sight of the machine working alongside them left the Haven‐62 survivors in awe.
They had many questions as well but Kai didn’t answer them since the operation time of Atom and other information related to it was top secret.
The enemies shouldn’t know the weakness of his Sentinel, even if there was none.
Hours of careful cataloguing had now paid off.
In any case, nothing was missing, but Kai couldn’t take everything...
He had to be satisfied for now.
Kai inspected the cars one last time, satisfied that the most important parts were secured.
"Let’s move," he ordered.
The gates of Haven‐62 creaked open, and soon, the convoy rolled out.
The survivors who had chosen to stay behind watched silently, while the eight new recruits sat inside the armored cars.
Soon, the group moved to Kai’s shelter.
The journey was uneventful, but that was what they prayed for...
Then, after some time, the familiar walls of New Haven‐45 came into view...
Of course, for Alfie, Farrah, and the six others, this would be their first time to see it... and the first thing they noticed was how terrifying it was!
"This..." Farrah was frozen.
As the armored cars rolled closer, they couldn’t help but feel nervous!
Along the walls of New Haven‐45 or Kai’s shelter, they saw rows of Sentinels!
They didn’t move, but their presence was enough to make the eight survivors uneasy.
Then, after passing through the gates, more Sentinels lined the pathways, standing at attention like silent soldiers!
"What?!
You’re controlling so many Sentinels?" Alfie muttered, his voice filled with disbelief.

chapters.title: Chapter 121: The Cost of Living in New Haven-45
paragraphs: The armored cars rolled through the gates, and the newcomers’ eyes stayed fixed on the rows of Sentinels standing tall along the walls and sides of the buildings...
Their unmoving posture made them look like soldiers frozen in time. It was such a fascinating and nerve-racking sight.
"What?! You’re controlling so many Sentinels?" Alfie muttered, his voice filled with disbelief.
Farrah’s lips parted, but no words came out.
She could only stare, stunned by the sight. Even the six others gulped nervously.
At this point, their imaginations were running wild.
Kai chuckled softly at their reaction. "Don’t be too impressed. These Sentinels aren’t functioning. I wouldn’t dare put batteries or Energy Cores in them."

The group turned to him, confused. Kai’s tone grew serious. "We have no way of controlling Sentinels. Atom is different... It’s special. If these units suddenly came online, the A.I. Rebel, Aria, might be able to connect to them and kill us. Even if she couldn’t connect due to signal issues, they’re still programmed to kill humans. There’s no chance I’d activate them."
He gestured toward the silent machines. "We already removed their batteries and emptied their cores. They’re just shells now. Useful for intimidation, but nothing more."
For a moment, the group went silent...
Then, one of the newcomers let out a shaky laugh.
"Whew... I almost pissed myself when I saw them standing there," he admitted, wiping sweat from his forehead.

Another survivor also heaved a sigh of relief while staring at the unmoving machines. "Even if they’re drained right now, it’s still amazing. These Sentinels, all lined up like soldiers... it makes this place feel untouchable."

A younger man also felt a lot more at ease and added. "Maybe you can reprogram them later? If Atom is special, maybe you can figure out how to make the others obey too. Imagine an army of Sentinels under your command..."
Farrah shook her head quickly. "Don’t even joke about that. If Aria connects to them online, we’re dead. Kai’s right not to risk it."

"Maybe find a way not to make them connect online or something? Just offline and reprogrammed robots. It’s possible when I’m activating pirated applications... I just have to do it offline or something." Alfie muttered softly.

He then paused for a moment before adding, "Still... I can’t lie. Just seeing them lined up like that makes me feel safer. Even if they’re empty, anyone who comes here will think twice before attacking."
Just like that, the group slowly relaxed... Even powerless, the Sentinels’ presence was intimidating and strangely reassuring at the same time.
Kai smirked faintly, watching their reactions.
Soon, Kai dropped them off at the main building.
"Come on. You’ve had a long day. Let’s get you something to eat."
He then led them toward the kitchen.
Introductions could be done later on anyway...
Inside, Rudy was on a short break, leaning against the counter.
Only two hours left, and he could leave this station.
However, as soon as he saw Kai, he straightened...
"Prepare meals for these eight," Kai instructed.
Rudy then moved without question, immediately preparing food for the eight newcomers.
"Wait... we already ate, Kai," Farrah said quickly, not wanting to burden the shelter’s supplies.
"Me too..." Alfie added, and the other six nodded in agreement.
First of all, Farrah and Alfie carried the Survivor Title.
[ Title: Survivor ]
[ Title Effect: Satiety decreases more slowly. Survivors can endure longer without food before hunger penalties occur. ]
Thanks to this title, they had no issues going without food for a day after eating once. They wouldn’t be at their strongest, but they could endure.

As for the six others, they had consumed gene enhancement serums, which allowed them to survive on very little food and water. They didn’t need to eat yet, having already filled their stomachs with beans and mushrooms back in Haven‐62.
Kai tilted his head slightly, amused.
He realized that they were worried about their supplies and it was something he’d appreciate.
"It’s fine. Supplies aren’t as tight as you think. Eat."
With that said, Rudy handed out granola bars first while preparing something warm.
He was currently alone, since Amer had already finished cooking earlier that morning.
"Granola bars? Haven’t had one of these in a while," one of them muttered as he opened the snack.
Another laughed softly. "Back in Haven‐62, we were lucky to get boiled beans. This feels like a feast already."
Rudy listened silently to their conversation as he moved quickly. Soon, he started cutting fresh moringa leaves from a basket, gathered from the small garden patch near the shelter.
He added them to a pot of instant noodles, letting the broth absorb their earthy flavor.
Then he opened a canned loaf, slicing it into thick pieces and dropping them into the pot, giving the meal a richer taste.
The smell filled the kitchen, comforting and familiar.
For survivors who had lived on scraps and mushrooms, it was almost overwhelming.
One of the six whispered, "This... smells better than anything we’ve had in weeks."
Rudy smiled after hearing this, but he didn’t respond. He simply worked as his focus was on the food.

Within minutes, steaming bowls of noodles were placed in front of the newcomers. The malunggay leaves floated on the surface, adding color and nutrition, while the canned loaf softened into the broth, making it hearty.
Farrah hesitated, then picked up her bowl. "Thank you," she said quietly.
Alfie followed, and soon the others did too.
Just like that, they ate slowly, savoring each bite.
"God... hot broth. I almost forgot what warmth feels like inside." One of them muttered in satisfaction.
"Meatloaf in noodles? Genius. It’s like we’re eating luxury. Thank you, Rudy!"
Soon, the warmth spread through their bodies, easing the tension of the journey.
After some time, Kai returned and watched them finish their meals.
By feeding them, he wasn’t just proving that New Haven 45 could provide, he was reminding them that this shelter must be protected.
Soon, the newcomers finished their bowls, some licking the last drops of broth.
It was at this point that Kai finally spoke.
"You’ll need to pay for that meal... and for the right to eat here every day. Just one Survivor Medal. With it, you and three of your companions can have three meals a day for two weeks."

chapters.title: Chapter 122: Prices
paragraphs: "Sorry... Did I hear it right?" Farrah asked as she replayed Kai’s words in her mind.
’We need to pay for the meal and the right to eat here every day? And that’s one Survivor Medal for me, and three of my companions, so we can have three meals a day for two weeks... What the--"
The words hit them like a hammer.
One of the six nearly spat out the last mouthful of noodles. Another froze, spoon halfway to his lips.
The group exchanged nervous glances, their faces pale.
"Wait... Are you serious?" Alfie asked with a trembling voice.
He was certainly willing to work for Kai, but the Survivor Medals were just too precious.
Farrah also frowned as she set her bowl down, staring at Kai.
"I don’t think we can pay that much. We need Medals to buy from the Gene Trader too. We have to get stronger if we want to contribute more to your shelter."
Alfie nodded and added, "Kai... Survivor Medals are too precious."
He didn’t say it, but Farrah only had seven, while he got six.
They were already lucky to have that many. At best, it means they could survive here for a few months if they’re careful.
The six residents of Haven‐62 looked even more disturbed.
One of them shook his head slowly. "We don’t even have access to Survivor Medals. We’re not... foreign survivors like you two. We’re people of this land. How can we contribute?"
The silence that followed was quite awkward.
However, Kai smiled at them after a few moments. He had expected this much.
"I know," he said calmly. "I was only teasing you."
The group blinked, stunned.
Kai chuckled and leaned back against the wall...

"At this early stage of the Apocalypse, Survivor Medals are far too precious. I wouldn’t waste them on meals. Instead, here’s what I expect... you’ll hand over every Energy Core you find. Furthermore, you’ll join us in raids and battles against the A.I. Army. That’s the real reasonable price of survival here..."
Although Kai wasn’t finished speaking, relief had already washed over the group.

Well, fighting the A.I. Army was no small feat. Still, compared to losing their Medals, it sounded almost generous, considering the fact that they were planning to defeat the A.I. Army in the first place.
Kai then continued...
"In return, you’ll eat once a day, plus a snack or light meal in the evening. That’s the standard ratio. For this much security, and the facilities you’ve seen here, it’s more than fair."
The six exchanged glances, then nodded quickly. "Yes... of course," one said. "That’s more than enough."
Another added, "We agree. Resources aren’t free. We understand."
Farrah exhaled slowly and finally relaxed her shoulders. "That’s... reasonable. Thank you, Kai."
Of course, Kai wasn’t done yet.

"But you have to remember that if the shelter’s condition improves... if the generator starts working, if more people arrive, if expenses start growing, then I will make it official. The Survivor Medal will be collected every month. That’s how we’ll sustain this place long‐term."
The group nodded again, some more reluctantly than others, but none dared argue.
Kai smiled at their reaction and nodded.
"Of course, if you donate Survivor Medals to me, you’ll receive resources in return. Supplies, tools, maybe even some enhancements. Donations will be rewarded."
That last part sparked interest.
Alfie wanted to clarify this...
"Donations? You mean... if we give you Medals, we can get things back other than the right to live here and eat free food?"
Kai nodded. "Exactly. Survivor Medals will become the most trusted currency. If you trust me with them, I’ll make sure you get something worthwhile."
Alfie rubbed his chin and nodded slowly. "It’s... fair. As long as we know what we’re getting."
Farrah paused for a moment as she considered what things she might actually need.
"So... if we donate Survivor Medals, what exactly can we get?"
Kai expected the question, but he had to be careful. He couldn’t overpromise them...
Furthermore, no one could know about his Infinite Gift Pack Talent.
Still, he could reveal just enough to spark their interest.

"Think of it as a set of items I can give you something similar to the Gift Packs that you encounter at the start of the Apocalypse," Kai said roughly. "Food like canned goods, instant noodles, granola bars, and mayonnaise. I can also supply you with revolvers together with its ammunition, smoke grenades, small tents, sleeping bags, folding bicycles, camouflage suits, and hatchets. Even medical kits..."
The room went quiet. The newcomers exchanged stunned glances. For people who had lived on scraps and mushrooms, the idea of structured supplies sounded almost too good to be true.
Alfie liked this a lot as he immediately spoke.
"Let’s say I donate one Survivor Medal. Can you give me... a revolver with thirty rounds of ammunition or maybe even more? Plus a free sleeping bag, a folding bicycle, and a camouflage suit?"
The others went silent as they also wanted to know Kai’s limit with this trade.
Farrah also waited, as no one could really tell her how valuable a Medal was. She had never seen the Gene Trader or what they could offer her.
Kai studied Alfie for a moment, then nodded slowly.
"Yes. I can give you that. And that’s not even enough... I will add more."
Alfie blinked. "More?"
Kai smiled as he began negotiating...
Well, he planned to be fair on this transaction since he had met the Gene Trader before.
For that person, one Survivor Medal could be exchanged for a Rapid Recovery Pill.
That particular pill was certainly precious, and if he would make a trade for that, he would be generous.

"Yes... If you’re willing to trust me with it, I’ll make sure you get more than just the basics. A revolver with thirty rounds is doable... A sleeping bag, a folding bicycle with a helmet, and a camouflage suit are also fine. But I’ll also throw in two smoke grenades, a firestarter, a flashlight with extra batteries, and a pocket knife." Kai said as he looked at the stunned group.

chapters.title: Chapter 123: Farming of Points
paragraphs: The group stared at Kai, knowing it was definitely a generous offer. They couldn’t miss this!
Since it was only a single Survivor Medal, Farrah believed that these items were worth the price since they weren’t easy to obtain in the first place.

Furthermore, they wouldn’t find any other Survivor who would be willing to do such a trade with them. Perhaps, Kai was the only one who could do this considering the fact that finding a Gene Trader wasn’t easy as well!
After all, the system had already mentioned before that the Gene Trader would be close to the Tyrants!
It meant that finding them could be extremely dangerous, and they already knew how strong those Tyrants were since one of them had almost annihilated their Haven-62.
It was only with Kai’s help that they managed to survive.
Without a doubt, this offer was definitely acceptable!
"That’s... generous... If that’s the case, I’ll also donate one Survivor Medal... But if possible, I want you to add night vision goggles and a few more smoke grenades..." Farrah immediately said.
Alfie smirked faintly at her boldness... "Always pushing for more, huh?"

Kai chuckled, shaking his head. "You drive a hard bargain. But yes, I can arrange that. Night vision goggles, extra smoke grenades... That’s doable. If you’re willing to donate, I’ll make sure you get what you need."
The six locals exchanged glances, envy flickering in their eyes. They had no Medals to offer, but watching Alfie and Farrah negotiate made them realize just how valuable those Medals were.
If they could help these two get those Medals, perhaps, they would also share whatever items they’d trade for them.
Kai’s gaze swept over them, and he decided to complete the transaction now.
"Then give me the Medals now."
Farrah and Alfie exchanged a glance, then opened their System Inventory.
A moment later, the metallic coins were placed in Kai’s hand.
They weren’t ordinary coins. Each was forged from copper or what seemed like one. They were also heavier than expected, and each of them was about two and a half inches in diameter.
Furthermore, the engraved human head on their surface seemed to stare back...
Kai closed his fist around the Medals, then gestured for them to follow.
"Come. I don’t keep supplies in the kitchen. We’ll go outside."
He led them out of the kitchen and across the courtyard to a smaller building. Inside, crates were stacked neatly, each marked and catalogued with the items Kai had stockpiled.
"Wait here..." Kai said, gesturing outside the building.
Soon, started opening one after another until he had gathered the promised items.
For Alfie’s Medal, Kai laid out a revolver with thirty rounds of ammunition.

Beside it, he placed a sleeping bag, a folding bicycle with its helmet, and a camouflage suit... It was exactly as Alfie had requested. Then, to keep the trade fair, Kai added two sturdy hatchets, a smoke grenade, and a compact medical kit.
After all, Farrah requested some additions as well.

Then, for Farrah’s Medal, Kai provided the same baseline package... A revolver with thirty rounds, a sleeping bag, a folding bicycle with a helmet, and a camouflage suit. Then, honoring her request for additions, he set down a pair of night vision goggles and three smoke grenades."
"Alright. Since the first transaction ever... I will reward you at the very least." Kai said as he also included a firestarter and a flashlight with spare batteries.
"These are yours," Kai said firmly.
Farrah’s eyes widened as she picked up the goggles. This was perfect for her. Alfie also tested the revolver’s weight and smiled in satisfaction.
"This feels nice..." Alfie admitted.
Soon, the group finally returned to the main building... Kai wanted to hand them over to Irene to give them a tour around the place.
However, before Kai could do so, a patrolman rushed in. He should be part of Wallace’s team.
"Sir Kai! Claire’s team is planning to visit the Gene Trader again. She wants to borrow one of the Armored Cars." The man said.
"I see... Wait for me..." Kai replied. Then, he noticed that these words shocked the two other Survivors.
"Ahhh, Did I not mention that we have access to one of the Gene Traders? Anyway... I’m planning to join Claire’s team. She’s one of the captains of the Assault Teams."
"We want to go too!"
"Please let us join!"
Kai looked at the two with a smile and nodded.
Just like that, the two armored cars left the shelter once again, and after a few minutes, they rumbled to a stop at the edge of the cemetery...
One car carried Claire’s Assault Team.
The other vehicle held Kai, Farrah, Alfie, and Atom...
As the doors opened, Kai stepped out first. His eyes swiftly scanned the ruined cemetery and confirmed that there was no one around.

"Alright," Kai said, turning to Farrah and Alfie. "Before we start farming for experience points, you two can go ahead and interact with the Gene Trader. You should be getting some achievement reward or something for meeting one and doing a transaction."
Farrah and Alfie exchanged a glance, confused by his phrasing.
Farming experience points?
It wasn’t something they had heard before, but Kai spoke with such certainty that they didn’t question it. Instead, they nodded and moved toward the broken mausoleum where the Gene Trader waited.
The figure inside was unsettling. He had a dark cloak and was surrounded by strange relics...
They weren’t sure if it was on purpose, but the Gene Trader’s presence radiated both opportunity and danger, sending a chill through them.
For a moment, Farrah felt her nerves tighten.
"Why does it have to look so terrifying?" she muttered.
Alfie grinned and lightened the mood. "Honestly, I’d be more suspicious if the Gene Trader looked like some cheerful beauty in a bikini. At least this way, we know it’s serious."
Farrah snorted before she finally stepped forward, ready to see what could be purchased.

They couldn’t miss this!
Since it was only a single Survivor Medal, Farrah believed that these items were worth the price since they weren’t easy to obtain in the first place.
Furthermore, they wouldn’t find any other Survivor who would be willing to do such a trade with them.
Perhaps, Kai was the only one who could do this considering the fact that finding a Gene Trader wasn’t easy as well!
After all, the system had already mentioned before that the Gene Trader would be close to the Tyrants!
It meant that finding them could be extremely dangerous, and they already knew how strong those Tyrants were since one of them had almost annihilated their Haven-62.
It was only with Kai’s help that they managed to survive.
Without a doubt, this offer was definitely acceptable!
"That’s... generous...
If that’s the case, I’ll also donate one Survivor Medal...
But if possible, I want you to add night vision goggles and a few more smoke grenades..." Farrah immediately said.
Alfie smirked faintly at her boldness...
"Always pushing for more, huh?"
Kai chuckled, shaking his head.
"You drive a hard bargain.
But yes, I can arrange that.
Night vision goggles, extra smoke grenades...
That’s doable.
If you’re willing to donate, I’ll make sure you get what you need."
The six locals exchanged glances, envy flickering in their eyes.
They had no Medals to offer, but watching Alfie and Farrah negotiate made them realize just how valuable those Medals were.
If they could help these two get those Medals, perhaps, they would also share whatever items they’d trade for them.
Kai’s gaze swept over them, and he decided to complete the transaction now.
"Then give me the Medals now."
Farrah and Alfie exchanged a glance, then opened their System Inventory.
A moment later, the metallic coins were placed in Kai’s hand.
They weren’t ordinary coins.
Each was forged from copper or what seemed like one.
They were also heavier than expected, and each of them was about two and a half inches in diameter.
Furthermore, the engraved human head on their surface seemed to stare back...
Kai closed his fist around the Medals, then gestured for them to follow.
"Come.
I don’t keep supplies in the kitchen.
We’ll go outside."
He led them out of the kitchen and across the courtyard to a smaller building.
Inside, crates were stacked neatly, each marked and catalogued with the items Kai had stockpiled.
"Wait here..." Kai said, gesturing outside the building.
Soon, started opening one after another until he had gathered the promised items.
For Alfie’s Medal, Kai laid out a revolver with thirty rounds of ammunition.
Beside it, he placed a sleeping bag, a folding bicycle with its helmet, and a camouflage suit...
It was exactly as Alfie had requested.
Then, to keep the trade fair, Kai added two sturdy hatchets, a smoke grenade, and a compact medical kit.
After all, Farrah requested some additions as well.
Then, for Farrah’s Medal, Kai provided the same baseline package...
A revolver with thirty rounds, a sleeping bag, a folding bicycle with a helmet, and a camouflage suit.
Then, honoring her request for additions, he set down a pair of night vision goggles and three smoke grenades."

I will reward you at the very least." Kai said as he also included a firestarter and a flashlight with spare batteries.

chapters.title: Chapter 124: Bug
paragraphs: While Farrah and Alfie were exploring the options that the Gene Trader could give, Kai walked toward Claire, who had just exited her armored car.
She adjusted her gloves and gave him a nod.
"Are those two new recruits?" she asked with a mysterious smile on her face.
"Yes," Kai replied. "They’re from Earth as well. They have strong close‐combat talents. Good frontliners."
Claire smiled, hearing this.
"That’s great news."
They certainly need some vanguards against the A.I. Soldiers, so she couldn’t help but appraise them from a distance.
"We’ll need more like them," she added.
Kai nodded and changed the topic. "So, are you planning to buy something again from the Trader? Make sure you’re not going to level down..."
He knew that she lacked Survivor Medals or Energy Cores. That means that her transactions must be through Experience Points only.
Claire couldn’t hide this from Kai and nodded. "Yes."
"You see... I remember he’s selling a perfume for three hundred experience points. I’m not going to level down yet anyway. I really want that."
Kai raised an eyebrow. "Perfume?"
Claire smirked.

"Don’t laugh. Think about it... most of these areas reek. Rotting corpses, stagnant water, sweat from people who haven’t had proper baths in weeks... even with clean water, body odor is everywhere." She then paused for a moment, confirming that Kai understood her.
’I can’t stop others from smelling bad, but I can at least fight against it for myself.’She said in her mind.
"Ahem... So a little perfume on my mask, my handkerchief, even my gloves... it makes a difference. It keeps me sane when I’m surrounded by the stench."

She shook her head, almost embarrassed. "The first time I saw it, I thought it was frivolous. Who cares about smelling nice when you’re fighting for survival? But after spending more time out here, I realized it’s not just for luxury... I can keep my senses sharp and not gag every time someone walks past, that’s worth the experience points."
Kai was stunned for a moment as he didn’t really expect such an answer.
However, that certainly made sense.
He then chuckled with understanding. "Haha... You’re right. Too bad we don’t have deodorant within the Gift Packs. I could’ve solved the problem if not for that."
Claire wryly smiled as she changed the topic.
"Are you planning to farm for Experience Points? We already sharpened our hatchets and prepared the revolvers. You’re helping us, right?"
Kai smiled knowingly. He had already thought of the same plan.
"Let’s do that after your trade. Go ahead."
Claire nodded and followed Farrah and Alfie into the dilapidated mausoleum.
Soon, the three emerged again, clutching their newly acquired items...
Now that the trades were complete, Kai gathered Farrah and Alfie near the armored car.

"Listen carefully. What we’re about to do isn’t simple. The Gene Trader’s territory is rigged with traps. When Survivors not from Earth step inside, it triggers waves of Mutants. Claire and I plan to use this to farm Experience Points."
Farrah blinked.
She finally understood Kai’s earlier words.
"Farm...? You mean deliberately summon them?"

Kai nodded. "Exactly. They’ll come in numbers, from hidden places you wouldn’t expect. Underground tunnels, broken buildings, even crypts. They don’t appear out of thin air, but still quite mysterious. This will be your first time, but stay sharp. Mutants can be annoying.
Alfie tightened his grip on his revolver and nodded. "We’re ready. Just tell us where to stand."
Kai’s lips curved faintly. He appreciated their resolve.
"Good. Stick close to Atom. He’ll cover you if things get overwhelming."
Atom, the Sentinel, stood silently nearby...
"Right..." Farrah and Alfie’s eyes lit up as soon as they recalled Atom!
The machine’s presence was reassuring now that they were on the same side!
For the next thirty minutes, the teams prepared.
Claire’s Assault Squad checked their weapons, making simple traps to control the advance, like putting wooden pikes, digging pitfalls, tying ropes that could trip, and other simple but useful tricks.
Farrah and Alfie adjusted their new camouflage suits from Kai. Then, they also tested the balance of their hatchets and revolvers. Kai oversaw everything and was satisfied with their preparations.
Finally, Claire raised her hand.
"Alright. Everyone’s ready... Trigger the traps."
One of her men stepped cautiously into the mausoleum’s threshold. The moment his foot crossed the boundary, the atmosphere changed.
A low rumble echoed beneath the cemetery, followed by the sound of stone cracking and metal grinding.
Then, chaos erupted.
Dozens of Mutants surged forth, clawing their way out of hidden tunnels and collapsing crypts. Some burst from beneath broken pavement, others from shattered mausoleums.
They were everywhere!
Farrah gasped, instinctively raising her revolver. "So many!"
"Focus! They’re coming from every direction. Hold the line!" Kai reminded.
Claire’s team immediately took the lead. They had fought Mutants before, and their experience showed.
Thanks to those battles, they had already adapted to the creatures’ speed and learned their attack patterns.
Soon, hatchets were swung, revolvers were fired, and smoke grenades detonated to shroud the battlefield!
The thick haze blinded the Mutants, forcing them to stumble into the traps the team had prepared.
Wooden pikes, hidden in the ground and angled for maximum impact, impaled several of the creatures as they charged recklessly forward!
Furthermore, the pitfalls and the ropes also slowed them down for an easier kill!
Just like that, the Mutants shrieked as their bodies collapsed under the coordinated assault!
Farrah and Alfie fought side by side, adrenaline surging through them.
"These things... are they even supposed to exist in the A.I. Apocalypse?!" Alfie shouted, firing his revolver and dropping a charging Mutant
"They should be in Zombie Outbreak or the Parasitic Evolution Apocalypse!" Farrah also complained...
However, it didn’t take that long before they changed their minds.
"So many experience points!" The two shouted in unison, forcing Kai to laugh.
They finally realized this was a blessing in disguise.
The only concern now was how long they could keep abusing this strange setting of mutant traps!
