Victor, on the other hand, was already satisfied with his ranking...
He really had to thank Kai for this opportunity.
After all, without this type of mutant farming, he’d just be staying in his workshop, and his Leveling would just halt in the process.
"I didn’t expect to be up there.
I mean, I’m just a mechanic.
Seeing my name among the top survivors feels... weird." He chuckled awkwardly, then added, "But hey, I’ll take it...
I hope I also get a nice Gene Skill after reaching Level 15."
Claire nudged him playfully.
"Weird?
You should be proud!
You’re practically famous now.
Everyone can see your name."
Victor groaned.
"I just hope we won’t get hunted by others for experience points.
It’s a good thing it was only showing our first names."
Just like that, the group couldn’t help but start a small celebration for their achievement.
Even though the rankings were just numbers, seeing their names displayed so prominently gave them a strange mix of pride, embarrassment, and determination to hold on to this ranking.
Soon, those who leveled up focus on the notifications they received from the system.
This time, Claire finally checked the long notifications she had received.
"Wow...
Kai.
So this is what you told us before.
I now have Reputation Points!
Just like what you said.
Only Level 15 and above can have them..." Claire said as she started checking her notifications.
Kai nodded.
"Yes...
But it’s a bit difficult getting them.
As far as I know, you can only get them from the first kill of C-Grade enemy units or higher, or some other achievements.
Well, maybe killing B-Grade enemy units will grant us better, but let’s not think about hunting them just yet."
For now, he wasn’t really worried about the number of Reputation Points that he had.
After all, he still had no idea how to use them or if being popular really had a value.
Perhaps getting higher Rep Points might even attract the attention of the A.I.
Army.
For now, Kai confirmed the notification of his latest level-up.
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ Level: 27 ]
[ Health Points +5 ]
[ Spirit Points +1 ]
[ Physique Rating Improved: C- ]
[ Inventory Slots Expanded: +1 ]
[ You have received an Instant Experience Potion x1 ]
"A free exp potion?" Kai muttered.
It was tempting to drink it right away, but Kai chose to save it for later.
Instead, he turned to the group.
"Burn the mutant corpses.
Rest, eat, and recover.
We’ll run the trap again once everyone’s ready."
The survivors cheered weakly, exhausted but thrilled with their activity...
Despite the blood and sweat, they had suffered only injuries... no casualties.
That made them confident to have another run.
"This is great...
Another round.
Let’s continue this until the Gene Trader leaves!" Claire shouted in celebration.
If possible, she wanted to reach Level 20 today!
"Experience Points farming for the win!
If we keep this up, I’ll hit Top 3 for sure!"

chapters.title: Chapter 146: The Rank 2 Survivor
paragraphs: They already used up all their Survivor Medals. They also didn’t have spare Energy Cores that they could use. Furthermore, none of them wanted to spend any more Experience Points to obtain some mundane items.
Everyone had the same intention as Claire! They all wanted to farm more experience points and level up, even if the Gene Trader vanished!
Ralph then reloaded his revolver before helping the others burn the mutants...
"Fine by me. More kills, more points. Just don’t fall behind, Claire. I’ll get more Experience Points later!"

Aurora sighed as she looked at her companions. They were all filled with energy... It was actually quite impressive. Although their health and spirit points reset after leveling up, they should still feel tired since their stamina does not reset at all.
In any case, she also helped with the cleaning...
Although nasty, she helped remove the mutants impaled on the traps they had set up.
Soon, she watched these mutants burn to ashes...

’They really crumble so fast... I wonder what’s making that happen.’ Aurora muttered after seeing these corpses burn like dried leaves. Even though she already knew the reason, the sight still amazed her every time.
After this, she assisted everyone in setting up the traps for the next batch of mutants.
Still, she couldn’t help but wonder why Kai’s leveling speed was too fast. After all, Kai’s mutant farming should be quite similar to theirs. The difference shouldn’t be this big.
However, he was now Level 27 for some reason.
’Is he getting more experience points than us? Wait... Is it because of Atom?’
Aurora’s eyes lit up as she realized this. ’Right... Atom isn’t human but a weapon. Since Kai is the owner, I guess the Experience Points go to him... That’s amazing.’
She also recalled Kai’s plan to revive the Sentinels in their base and put them under his control.
If that really happened, Kai would surely maintain his current Rank in the Leaderboard.
’It’s a good thing I sided with him... That foolish Terrence. He can’t read the situation properly.’She mused.
Although she was only eighteen, she was confident in her interpersonal skills. Over the past few days, she had carefully observed everyone’s behavior and learned their personalities.
A couple of weeks ago, she was already aware that Terrence wasn’t showing his true self. Because of that, she knew that she had to avoid him.
So, when Kai accepted her group along with Terrence and Jonas, she immediately distanced herself from Terrence. She cut off any unnecessary connection and only spoke to him when absolutely necessary.
After some time, they continued on their mission...
They triggered the traps twice more!
Each round brought another wave of shrieking mutants, and of course, the survivors fought with their traps, guns, blades, and their desire to level up!
The pitfalls were filled with corpses again, the trip wires stopped the advancing mutants, and the planted wooden and metal pikes impaled them like before.
By the end of the third attempt, however, fatigue had set in.
Their arms felt heavy, their blades had already dulled, and every revolver clicked empty... not a single bullet remained in their stocks.
Thankfully, they already had a bunch of experience on this matter, so aside from six people getting heavily injured, none of them had actually perished!
"We’re done here..." Kai muttered, seeing how everyone looked happy but also tired.
Furthermore, they couldn’t continue because, as expected, the Gene Trader had already vanished, and without its presence, the mutant lure no longer worked.
Still, the effort had paid off. Many of them had leveled up two or even three times, their names climbing higher on the Leaderboard.
Kai, however, only advanced once more, reaching Level 28. Even so, his steady progress kept him far ahead of the others.
"Let’s clean up the place!" Kai said...
"Yes! Let’s finish this quickly and go home."
"Where’s my lighter?"
"As for the ones in the pitfalls, just throw some burning leaves. That’s more than enough. They’ll burn fast..."
Just like that, Kai oversaw the cleanup.
He watched as the corpses burned to ash, then removed the metal pikes himself, knowing their value for future traps.
Of course, he’d let Atom carry these traps for him...
The wooden structures, however, were left in place since they were just disposable tools.
With the battlefield cleared, the weary survivors finally turned back toward their shelter, eager for rest after a long day of battle...
Meanwhile, not too far from New Haven Shelter-45, Renji crouched near the broken window of a sixth-floor apartment as he scanned the streets below.
The last time he checked the Leaderboard, he was still the Rank 2 Survivor after reaching Level 16.
However, after his snack this afternoon, he realized that he was already at Rank 6!
’Tsk... I just relaxed for a bit, and I’m being left behind. I have to find more Sentinels.’Renji thought, realizing he hadn’t been pushing himself hard enough.
Unfortunately, the abandoned city stretched out in silence. He wasn’t hearing any more patrols or movements from Sentinels.
He saw the cracked pavement already swallowed by vines and moss. Nature was reclaiming what the machines had left behind...
Soon, he heard some drones passing through and wryly smiled. He didn’t want anything to do with Swarmers, and they’re just too difficult to deal with.
Anyway, he had been the lone survivor of Haven-32, the settlement that fell during the Mech Siege.
Everyone else had been slaughtered or buried alive... but Renji had escaped with nothing but his wits and the strange gift the system had granted him, an Epic-Grade Talent called Mechanical Expert.
That talent had saved his life more than once.
It gave him an instinctive understanding of machines, a way to dismantle, rebuild, and reprogram them as if he had been born for it.
And it was the reason his name now sat at Rank 2 on the Leaderboard, despite not having a large team that could farm for experience points like Kai.
Apparently, after leaving Haven-32, Renji had avoided the forests.
There were too many A.I. patrols sweeping the wilderness. After all, they’re probably expecting the survivors hiding from the CCTVs or drones of the Mech Army.
Because of that, he had chosen the abandoned city instead... Although he still believed that survivors might be hiding in basements, sewers, or forgotten tunnels, there shouldn’t be a lot of them.
Unfortunately, his guess was wrong. There was no hidden shelter here at all!
The city was empty. He found no other humans or allies. Just ruins!
Still, he was quite lucky...
What he found instead, buried in a junkyard are two androids, both about his height, designed with slim frames that mimicked human women.
Their bodies were scratched, their joints were broken, but their cores were intact.
With his spare Energy Cores, he was confident that he could repair them.
But at first, Renji hesitated. Repairing them could be suicide. If Aria, the A.I. Rebel, ever reconnected them to the network, they would turn on him instantly.
Nonetheless, after studying the machines for a few days, his talent allowed him to understand better...
With his Mechanical Expert Talent, he could sever their online capabilities, cut off their wireless receivers, and make them immune to remote control.
The only way to hack them now would be through direct, physical access.
So he took the risk.
The repairs were ugly at first. One android had a blade strapped in place of an arm. The other balanced awkwardly on a wooden leg.
Their movements were irregular and they could only make some odd noise when acknowledging his orders.
But at the very least, they obeyed his commands. They help him fight and destroy enemy units!
Renji named them Android 9 and Android 18, his favorite numbers.
Day after day, he scavenged parts from ruined factories and dismantled Sentinels...
Slowly, their bodies improved. The wooden leg was replaced with steel plating. The blade-arm was reforged into a proper limb. Their sensors sharpened and their combat efficiency grew.
Together, they became his strike team.
While Kai farmed mutants with traps and teamwork, Renji hunted machines with his newfound allies...
Android 9 and 18 tore through Sentinels, ambushed Swarmers, and dismantled Hounds as Renji was slowly making a mount for his androids...
Of course, he himself scavenged weapons from the wreckage.
From one raid, he stole three plasma rifles, each fully charged with energy cores!
Renji’s days were simple... At dawn, he scouted rooftops, marking the routes of the Sentinels.
Then, by noon, he sent Android 9 and 18 to attack enemy units while he sniped from above with plasma fire if necessary.
At night, he returned to his hideout, repairing their frames with whatever scraps he had found.
The androids never spoke, but Renji talked to them anyway.
"Good work, 9. Keep your guard up."
"18, you’re too reckless. Look at your shoulder. Watch your flanks, you dummy... Don’t let them circle us."
"Another patrol down. That’s three cores today. We’re getting stronger."
His voice filled the silence of the city.
Sometimes, he caught himself imagining they could respond.
He wondered what it would be like if they had personalities, if they could laugh or argue like humans.
But as he imagined that life, he suddenly froze after hearing a buzzing sound.
As he looked through the window, he saw it...
A huge mechanized city flying in the sky!

chapters.title: Chapter 147: The World Chat
paragraphs: Renji froze in shock as the shadow of the massive flying fortress drifted above him...
’What in the world? Isn’t this supposed to be a Rebellion of human-made Artificial Intelligence? Why does it feel like I entered Alien Invasion? This is cheating!’
He couldn’t imagine himself standing against that thing!
Still, he could only complain in silence as he didn’t want to get noticed by that thing in the sky.
The mechanized citadel was just too intimidating!
Its engines were rumbling like thunder, and he could also see numerous weapons or barrels of cannons sticking out everywhere.
Of course, it was the same fortress Kai’s group had seen before.
For a moment, Renji felt small.
His androids stood silently behind him as they were probably trying to understand what they were seeing in the sky.
’Just don’t drop some Tyrants or some other huge mechs...’
Renji clenched his fists as he stared in the direction the fortress was heading.
"Wait... That’s probably where the A.I. base is located... or maybe something important is happening there," he mused.
He knew one thing for certain... If the system had truly sent them here to end the apocalypse, then hiding in ruins would never be enough. Sooner or later, he would have to go where the enemies were.
Because of that, he observed the flying fortress carefully as he considered the path it was taking.
If it was heading to a Human Shelter or maybe to another A.I. Base to refuel, he wanted to know where it was exactly...
After all, if it was actually trying to attack another shelter, then that place would soon become a battlefield. He might find some important things there that he could scavenge.
But if it was moving to reinforce another A.I. stronghold, then following it might reveal their next target.
Either way, it was important.
"Hu~ I need to be patient... I can do this." As he said this, the flying fortress was already in the horizon... and it didn’t drop any Tyrants or Sentinels!
"Nice..."

Renji knew that he wasn’t strong enough yet. His androids were powerful, but crude. His plasma rifles were precious, but limited. Still, his Mechanical Expert talent gave him an edge. If he could scavenge more, repair faster, and keep building, he might stand a chance and reach the higher level soon.
Renji then turned to Android 9 and 18.
At a glance, they looked almost human now. Their faces had synthetic skin, giving them the appearance of young women with impressive features.
They had black hair that fell unevenly to their shoulders, and blue eyes that were quite charming. Their designer or previous owner must have spent a lot of time designing their faces.
Of course, most of their synthetic skin was already gone when he found these two in the junkyard.
There were even remnants of their burned human‐skin covers at that time. But he had already stripped away those useless synthetic skins and left the ones on their faces.
In short, all other body parts were just raw machinery beneath. To hide this, Renji had wrapped their exposed joints and body in cloth and bandages, covering most of their mechanical frames.
"We’re not staying here. We’ll follow that fortress."
The humanoid machines or androids didn’t respond, but their optic lights blinked as if acknowledging his command.
They seemed to have problems with their programming or it was just designed to be like that.
Anyway, Renji took one last look at the fortress as it drifted farther away. It would be interesting if he managed to enter that place and destroy it from the inside.
It would probably give him a huge amount of experience points, and most likely, he’d be able to surpass Kai!
But he knew better. He knew how weak he was right now and had to work harder!
Just like that, he continued with his daily life while also slowly moving towards the path that the Flying Fortress had taken.
Every machine he destroyed fed him full Experience Points. Unlike Kai’s team, he didn’t split rewards.
With 9 and 18, he fought like a squad, but the system counted them as his extensions. Their kills were his kills!

Furthermore, with stolen high-grade weapons, he could take down stronger units than most survivors dared to face. It was unfortunate that he couldn’t charge the Plasma Rifles easily, but still, he was off to a good start.

Then, with his Mechanical Expert talent, he dismantled the Mechanized Soldiers and converted scraps into usable gear. Every raid gave him more than just experience... it gave him resources for him and his two androids!
This was why Renji had climbed from Level 16 to Level 20 in such a short time.
He wasn’t farming mutants. He was dismantling the A.I. Army itself!
Still, as soon as he reached Level 20, he obtained incredible rewards!
[ New Feature Activated: World Chat ]
[ Description: Survivors who reach Level 20 gain access to the World Chat system. Communicate across shelters and territories. ]
[ Limit: 3 messages per day. ]
[ Warning: Messages are visible to all Level 20 Survivors worldwide. Use wisely. ]
Renji blinked as the system notification appeared before his eyes.
"A world chat! This is awesome! Now, we can share information..."
Without hesitation, he opened the World Chat Feature!
The first thing he noticed was the latest message.
[ System: Renji has entered the chat. ]
"Ohhh... It’s welcoming me..." Renji muttered with a laugh. "This is so cool!"
Then, a faint glow spread across his vision, and a mystical keyboard materialized in front of him. He hesitated for a moment, then tapped out his first message.
[ Renji: I’m from Haven‐32. It’s already destroyed, and I’m just wandering around. Are we in the same area? ]
The words vanished into the ether, instantly broadcast to every Level 20 survivor worldwide.
Scrolling upward, Renji saw the earlier conversations.
As expected, Kai and Claire had already been chatting.
Their exchanges weren’t particularly meaningful...
To Renji, it was nonsense. But it gave him a hint of the situation.
It told him something important... Kai and Claire were close. Maybe even together.
[ Claire: Ugh, I’m starving. If only the Gene Trader sold snacks. ]
[ Kai: Snacks? You’d waste experience points on chips? ]
[ Claire: Better than wasting them on those traps you bought. ]
[ Kai: My traps are beautiful. Don’t insult them. ]

They were just using two messages per day... Well, they were only allowed for three chats per day, so they were probably saving one for important matters while using the other two, since they would just reset anyway.
Further down, just above his notification that he entered the chat, another name caught his attention... Mei.
She had only just entered the chat, and her first message was blunt...
[ Mei: Kai... can you tell me your full name? ]

It was unfortunate that he couldn’t charge the Plasma Rifles easily, but still, he was off to a good start.
Then, with his Mechanical Expert talent, he dismantled the Mechanized Soldiers and converted scraps into usable gear.
Every raid gave him more than just experience... it gave him resources for him and his two androids!
This was why Renji had climbed from Level 16 to Level 20 in such a short time.
He wasn’t farming mutants.
He was dismantling the A.I.
Army itself!
Still, as soon as he reached Level 20, he obtained incredible rewards!
[ New Feature Activated: World Chat ]
[ Description: Survivors who reach Level 20 gain access to the World Chat system.
Communicate across shelters and territories. ]
[ Limit: 3 messages per day. ]
[ Warning: Messages are visible to all Level 20 Survivors worldwide.
Use wisely. ]
Renji blinked as the system notification appeared before his eyes.
"A world chat!
This is awesome!
Now, we can share information..."
Without hesitation, he opened the World Chat Feature!
The first thing he noticed was the latest message.
[ System: Renji has entered the chat. ]
"Ohhh...
It’s welcoming me..." Renji muttered with a laugh.
"This is so cool!"
Then, a faint glow spread across his vision, and a mystical keyboard materialized in front of him.
He hesitated for a moment, then tapped out his first message.
[ Renji: I’m from Haven‐32.
It’s already destroyed, and I’m just wandering around.
Are we in the same area? ]
The words vanished into the ether, instantly broadcast to every Level 20 survivor worldwide.
Scrolling upward, Renji saw the earlier conversations.
As expected, Kai and Claire had already been chatting.
Their exchanges weren’t particularly meaningful...
To Renji, it was nonsense.
But it gave him a hint of the situation.
It told him something important...
Kai and Claire were close.
Maybe even together.
[ Claire: Ugh, I’m starving.
If only the Gene Trader sold snacks. ]
[ Kai: Snacks?
You’d waste experience points on chips? ]
[ Claire: Better than wasting them on those traps you bought. ]
[ Kai: My traps are beautiful.
Don’t insult them. ]
They were just using two messages per day...
Well, they were only allowed for three chats per day, so they were probably saving one for important matters while using the other two, since they would just reset anyway.
Further down, just above his notification that he entered the chat, another name caught his attention...
Mei.
She had only just entered the chat, and her first message was blunt...
[ Mei: Kai... can you tell me your full name? ]

chapters.title: Chapter 148: High Level
paragraphs: "Hmm?" Renji stared at Mei’s message.
He was curious why Mei wanted to know Kai’s full name... After all, it didn’t seem like an appropriate greeting.
He could only guess that Mei knew someone with that first name back from Earth.
However, although she wanted information, Kai was smart enough not to reply.
After all, Mei could be an enemy who was gathering information. It was better not to give too much information about yourself.
Of course, it was also possible that Kai hadn’t read the chat yet, instead of deliberately ignoring it.
Still, Renji couldn’t help but realize the usefulness of this World Chat.
It wasn’t just a place for idle talk. It was a window into alliances, rivalries, and secrets.
They could use this platform gifted by the system to their advantage against the A.I. Army!
’There’s no way Aria will be able to hack this system, right?’Renji mused.
Now it was his turn.
He looked at his message.
Well, his chat hung in the feed, waiting for replies.
Would anyone recognize Haven‐32? Would they be friendly? Or would they dismiss him as just another wanderer?
Renji’s eyes turned toward Android 9 and 18.
"Let’s see who answers," he muttered.
"This might be the start of something bigger."
Renji finally relaxed as he waited to see who would respond.
Unfortunately, the chat feed remained quiet even after some time... He wasn’t even greeted back by these people who were above Level 20!
With a sigh, Renji just checked the Leaderboard and noticed Kai’s name sitting higher on the Leaderboard.
He had advanced again and reached Level 30.
"I wonder if there’s a new System Feature activated at that Level..." He mused.
A couple of days ago, Kai finally reached Level 30. It was just in time before the month ends for the monthly ranking rewards.
Of course, this level hadn’t happened through farming mutants with Gene Trader traps like before. Instead, it came in various Sentinel Hunts and from something unexpected...
Well, the last few hundred experience points were thanks to his return to Haven‐45 Shelter, the very first shelter where the system had transported him.
The place was still a dumpsite.
Organic waste, broken scraps, and discarded materials were piled high, rotting under the sun.
Kai had only gone there to look around, but what he found there helped him finally reach the last few hundred Experience Points that he needed.
Apparently, an automated garbage hauler rolled into the area.
It was the familiar garbage truck...
Kai watched its mechanical arms tossing junk into the pit.
But it wasn’t alone. Two Sentinels guarded it as expected.
"Haha! Got you!" Kai laughed as he finally saw these moving Experience Points!
Kai didn’t hesitate.
With Atom at his side, he launched the attack.
"Let’s go, Atom! They’re only holding normal rifles! We can do this fast! Take care of the one on the left!
Just like that, Atom advanced on the first Sentinel... Bang! Bang! Bang!
The Sentinel shot upon seeing Atom, but its rifle was only good against humans!
It was useless against an A-Grade Sentinel!

Soon, Atom managed to get closer and its blade cut three times in succession! The first strike severed the machine’s shoulder joint, the second sliced across its torso, and the third pierced straight through its chest unit!
Thud! Thud! Thud!
The Sentinel’s body convulsed as its core was destroyed! Its circuit board was filled with sparks before it collapsed in silence.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (D) ]
[ +410 Experience Points ]
The second Sentinel, realizing that the guns weren’t working against Atom, raised its blade instead...
However, Kai was already closed!
He had actually used Atom as a bait to get their attention!
Furthermore, he activated Specter Step.
[ Gene Skill Activated: Specter Step ]
Spirit Points: -20
His body moved forward, leaving behind a faint afterimage. In less than a heartbeat, he had repositioned to its flank.
Kai thrust out his hand.
[ Gene Skill Activated: Spirit Pulse ]
Spirit Points: -70
A burst of Spirit Energy erupted, slamming into the Sentinel’s body!
Boom!
The controlled shockwave disrupted its balance, forcing its systems to malfunction!
Kai then closed in with his hatchet raised!
"It’s here..."
His Keen Sense guided him and found the battery cell buried inside the machine.
Ha!
Crash!
With a powerful swing, the cell cracked, releasing a violent discharge of light!
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (D) ]
[ +410 Experience Points ]
At the same time, he finally reached Level 30 and was flooded with notifications!
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ Level: 30 ]
[ Health Points +100 ]
[ Spirit Points +5 ]
[ Physique Rating has greatly improved! ]
"Whoaaa~ Finally!"
Kai felt incredibly happy as he felt a surge of power. He had finally reached another milestone!
There were a lot of things he needed to check. Still, Kai carefully checked the remaining messages.
[ Congratulations! You are the first Survivor to reach Level 30! ]
[ You have received: Instant Experience Potion ×5, Energy Cores (C) ×10, Random Gift Pack ×5, Material Treasure Chest ×2, Random Gene Skill Crystal (Mid‐Grade) ]
[ Congratulations! You have reached the limit of your physique’s current potential. ]
[ You have received: Reputation Points +10, Skill Points +3 ]

"Ughh... So that’s why... I already reached the limit of Spirit Points and Health Points... I must change something with my physique to get past the limit, huh." Kai muttered. He felt quite disappointed about this as he recalled the items he had purchased from the Gene Trader.
In any case, the notification hadn’t ended yet.
Just like what happened at Level 20, a new feature was activated at Level 30!
[ New Feature Activated: Guild ]

[ Description: Survivors who reach Level 30 gain access to the Guild system. Guilds are organized survivor groups that allow members to share resources, coordinate strategies, and grow stronger together. ]
[ Requirement: Payment of 10 Survivor Medals to establish a Guild. ]
[ Limit: Each Guild may recruit up to 50 members. ]
[ Benefit: All Guild members receive a passive buff depending on Guild Level. Guild Chat, Guild Storage, Guild Missions, and Guild Reputation will be unlocked once you create or join a Guild. ]
"Seriously..." Kai muttered as he saw the notifications in front of him.

chapters.title: Chapter 149: Bound
paragraphs: Kai still had spare Survivor Medals with him, thanks to the other Foreign Survivors within New Haven-45. They would pay him a Survivor Medal in exchange for bullets, food, and other items that he could offer, and he was quite generous about it.
After all, everyone knew the value of a single Survivor Medal.

Because of that, he could immediately create a Guild. However, he was a bit skeptical about whether he should do it now or wait for a bit. After all, there might be some other important things he could do with his Medals.
But then, he realized something...
’Wait... I can’t waste the chance of getting a reward for having created the first Guild. I’m sure there’s a reward to that.’Kai thought as he had pretty much read how the system works already.
He then opened his inventory as he finally checked the number of Experience Potions that he had.

He had been collecting them all this time and barely using them for occasions like this. He knew from experience that reaching milestone levels, Level 10, Level 20, and now Level 30, required far more experience points than ordinary levels.
Back then, breaking through to Level 11 and Level 21 had been far more difficult than climbing from 11 to 12 or 21 to 22. The system always made the first step past a milestone the hardest.
That was why he had saved these potions.
He knew Level 30 would demand an enormous amount of experience to push him toward the next stage.
"So I have ten of these already... Nice."
[ Item: Instant Experience Potion x10 ]
[ Description: Grants 5,500 Experience Points upon consumption. ]
[ Quantity: 10 ]
Kai pulled them out, hoping he wouldn’t need to use them all at once.
Each vial was small, holding no more than ten milliliters of deep blue liquid.
Without hesitation, Kai uncorked the first vial and drank.
The liquid burned down his throat, leaving a cold aftertaste.
[ +5,500 Experience Points ]
He didn’t stop. One after another, he consumed them, ignoring the bitterness.
The system notifications stacked rapidly in front of him, each one confirming another surge of points.
By the ninth potion, Kai paused with a frown...
"That’s 49,500 experience points already..." he muttered.

He shook his head. A single D‐Grade Sentinel gave 410 points. That meant he had just gained the equivalent of killing 120 Sentinels in minutes. The sheer efficiency of these potions was staggering, but it also reminded him how impossible leveling would be without Atom or his raids.
If he just relied on killing Sentinels, it would take too long. However, if he relied on his precious Gene Enhancement Serums, it would be such a huge waste!
After all, everyone knew that Gene Enhancement Serums provided improvement in his physique, small amounts of Experience Points, with extra Health and Spirit Points.
However, after consuming a certain amount of them, his Physique would no longer improve. Then, his Health and Spirit Points would also stop increasing.

Of course, he would still gain a little amount of Experience Points, but that would be too wasteful since all its other effects would be useless. If he had to consume the Gene Enhancement Serums, it had to happen after breaking through his Physical Limits where he could accept more Gene Enhancements.
He then raised the last vial, hesitated for a moment, and then drank it down.
[ +5,500 Experience Points ]
This time, the system didn’t simply add the points. The next notification made him feel really excited!
[ Experience Limit Reached! ]
Kai’s eyes widened as he saw this.
"So I reached the cap... I might have wasted five thousand points just now."
Well, he probably wasted 5,000 Experience Points, as the limit might’ve been 50,000, but it didn’t matter now.
The system message expanded, revealing the details of his next step.
[ Breakthrough Requirement: To advance beyond Level 30, the Survivor must complete a special quest. ]
[ Quest: Strengthen your foundation.
Possess at least 5 Gene Skills upgraded to Level 5.
Absorb 10 B‐Grade Energy Cores.
Bind 3 Gene Weapons to your body. ]
[ Reward: Unlock Physique Evolution. Gain access to advanced stat growth and new Gene Skill compatibility. ]
[ Survivor will remain capped at Level 30 until the requirement is fulfilled. ]
Kai was stunned as he saw the requirements he must fulfill.
Five Gene Skills reaching Level 5 was possible for him. After all, his mastery increased quickly thanks to his title. That part would only take time.
But absorbing ten B‐Grade Energy Cores? That was far more difficult. Those cores were rare, and where the heck would he even get one? C-Grade Energy Cores from Tyrants were already hard to get.

As for the Gene Weapons... he already had three of them, but none were bound to his body yet. He just kept them in his inventory. After all, he was still hesitating whether he should bind Low-Grade Gene Weapons or wait for a higher grade.
With Althea and Sera’s prior knowledge about Gene Weapons, he knew that these weapons were bound to the user.
You couldn’t just throw them away if you no longer needed them.
With this in mind, Kai obviously decided to be careful on this matter.
Kai could only sigh as he looked around the filthy surroundings.
Soon, he noticed the automated garbage truck still dumping trash into the pit.
"Ohhh... You’re still here, huh."
His eyes lit up. He hadn’t destroyed it earlier, and now he moved quickly to inspect it.
With no Sentinels left guarding the vehicle, he was free to do whatever he wanted... and of course, he robbed it.
He pried open its compartments and discovered several spare energy cells, the kind used by D‐Grade Sentinels.
They weren’t true Energy Cores, since these were manufactured by Aria rather than the A.I. Civilization. Still, they were valuable.
For Kai’s shelter, this was a treasure trove. With these cells, they could power appliances, lights, and even reinforce some defensive systems.
Victor really wanted to add those electric fences... Anyway, it would be useful with the right people.
Then, rather than dismantling the vehicle, Kai let it continue its route and followed it with Atom, keeping a careful distance.
"Now... let’s see where your base is," he muttered, as the truck moved deeper into unknown territory.

chapters.title: Chapter 150: Everyone’s Vices and Kai’s Discovery
paragraphs: In the meantime, while Kai was enjoying his time outside the shelter, the afternoon in New Haven‐45 was quiet.
There were no alarms, gunfire, or mechanized soldiers trying to attack them. At this time, the shelter felt almost normal.
"I want something new..." Claire muttered as she sat at one of the long wooden tables in the mess hall...
Soon, she peeled open an MRE packet she had saved in her inventory.

Earlier, she had only eaten instant noodles with a handful of moringa leaves and two slices of meatloaf. It was certainly enough to fill her for the day, but since it was peaceful, she treated herself.
She unfolded the menu card inside the MRE and smiled.
[ Menu: Beef Stew, Crackers, Cheese Spread, Chocolate Bar, Instant Coffee ]
It wasn’t gourmet, but compared to noodles, it felt like luxury.
"Nice... I got a nice menu today..."
She heated the beef stew pouch over a small portable warmer, tore open the crackers, and spread the cheese across them.
She was quite used to this already.
Then, she turned her attention to the chocolate bar. It was a welcome surprise, and it made her think back to her days on Earth.
"Not bad," she murmured, chewing slowly.
She had always loved her favorite brand, Hercheese. This bar wasn’t nearly as good, but it still gave her a taste she had almost forgotten. For that, she was thankful.
As for the coffee, she saved it for later.
As soon as the meal was ready, she immediately tasted a spoonful of it...
"Mhmmm..."
The stew was salty, but it had real chunks of meat and potatoes. She liked it more than she expected.
After finishing her meal, Claire pulled out her old digicam, the one she purchased from the Gene Trader.
She scrolled through the photos she had taken over the past few days...
There were pictures of the Sentinels they had destroyed, the shelter walls patched with scavenged steel, and candid shots of her friends...
Many of them were Marissa laughing with Aurora, Victor tinkering with tools, Wallace posing with his usual grin. They all looked good in the pictures, despite the harsh life they lived.
Soon, she noticed that the battery icon blinked red, showing only one bar left.
She sighed. "I’ll have to replace this soon."
Luckily, Kai had stocked the warehouse with spare batteries for everyone’s devices.
That warehouse was a treasure in itself.

Shane managed the trades there, exchanging items for Survivor Medals. Inside were sleeping bags, tents, bicycles, helmets, camouflage suits, hatchets, and countless other supplies. It was the kind of place that reminded Claire how much Kai had done to keep them prepared.
After cleaning the table, she planned to visit the greenhouse next, where mushrooms, peanuts, and herbs were being cultivated.
The small field had become one of their most important areas, giving them fresh food beyond canned goods and MREs.
But on her way, she stopped short.
"Huh?"
Wallace was leaning against a wall, holding a cigarette between his fingers.
Two locals, Althea and Sera, stood nearby, awkwardly copying his movements.
"The heck?"
Claire frowned.
She recalled that Wallace had actually purchased ten packs of cigarettes using his Experience Points, and now he was trying to teach the girls how to smoke.
She walked closer and looked at the man as if he were an idiot.
"Wallace, really? Do you two even know the side effects of those things?" she asked, looking at Althea and Sera.
The cigarettes that the Gene Trader had given smelled really stronger compared to the ones back on Earth. She was worried that they would have worse effects on human bodies.
Wallace chuckled, exhaling a thin stream of smoke.

"Relax, Claire. We’ve all consumed Gene Enhancement Serums. Especially these two young women. They even have Gene Weapons before we could have one. The usual side effects don’t apply to them. Their lungs... their bodies can handle it."
Claire shook her head. "That doesn’t mean it’s good for them. You’re wasting points on something that doesn’t help anyone."
"Heh... This helps me calm down, you know?" Wallace said as he recalled his days back on Earth.
Claire sighed as she couldn’t really prohibit the man from getting these two girls addicted to smoking. They were already old enough to know better.
Right now, however, Althea looked uncertain, lowering the cigarette. Sera also laughed nervously, clearly unsure if she should continue.
Claire softened her tone and waved her hand.
"Alright... Just don’t smoke near Aurora’s field. She is growing our food there."
Wallace blinked and tilted his head, confused.
"Isn’t it better to smoke near plants? If I smoke near the plants, they’ll absorb some of it... Doesn’t it clean the air or something?"
Claire paused, then shook her head firmly.
"That’s not how it works. The smoke doesn’t disappear... It sticks. Do you really want your moringa leaves, cabbage, and string beans tasting like cigarettes?"
Althea wrinkled her nose at the thought, while Sera laughed awkwardly, putting out the cigarette Wallace had handed her.
Wallace shrugged, grinning. "Fine, fine. I’ll keep it away from the crops. But don’t expect me to quit anytime soon."
Claire sighed, relieved she had at least kept the smoke away from their food.
"I know... Everyone’s got their own vices."
She decided not to push further.
She wasn’t a busybody, but she couldn’t ignore it either.
With a shake of her head, she left them behind and continued toward the greenhouse...
In the meantime, Kai was still following the garbage hauler, and soon, he discovered a hidden base!
It wasn’t a massive A.I. city, but it was large enough to rival a village.
"Finally... Another target! Maybe I can get ten B-Grade Cores here!"
However, as he continued observing from afar using his Keen Sense, he froze for a moment...
He expected to find more machines, but what he saw made his blood run cold.
Humans.
Dozens of them, chained and forced to work under the watch of A.I. soldiers!

There were no alarms, gunfire, or mechanized soldiers trying to attack them.
At this time, the shelter felt almost normal.
"I want something new..." Claire muttered as she sat at one of the long wooden tables in the mess hall...
Soon, she peeled open an MRE packet she had saved in her inventory.
Earlier, she had only eaten instant noodles with a handful of moringa leaves and two slices of meatloaf.
It was certainly enough to fill her for the day, but since it was peaceful, she treated herself.
She unfolded the menu card inside the MRE and smiled.
[ Menu: Beef Stew, Crackers, Cheese Spread, Chocolate Bar, Instant Coffee ]
It wasn’t gourmet, but compared to noodles, it felt like luxury.
"Nice...
I got a nice menu today..."
She heated the beef stew pouch over a small portable warmer, tore open the crackers, and spread the cheese across them.
She was quite used to this already.
Then, she turned her attention to the chocolate bar.
It was a welcome surprise, and it made her think back to her days on Earth.
"Not bad," she murmured, chewing slowly.
She had always loved her favorite brand, Hercheese.
This bar wasn’t nearly as good, but it still gave her a taste she had almost forgotten.
For that, she was thankful.
As for the coffee, she saved it for later.
As soon as the meal was ready, she immediately tasted a spoonful of it...
"Mhmmm..."
The stew was salty, but it had real chunks of meat and potatoes.
She liked it more than she expected.

She scrolled through the photos she had taken over the past few days...

She sighed.
